 Oklahoma's win over the Rebels highlighted how roster turnover and free agency have killed longstanding traditions
 By
 Zach Dean Fox News 
 Published

 On today's episode of Don't @ Me with Dan Dakich, Dan roasts Lane Kiffin after Alabama walked into Death Valley and handed the Tigers an embarrassing 31-13 beatdown, dropping LSU to 6-3 with Texas and Tennessee looming.
 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com . 
 Third Monday of November, folks. Hard to believe, but we're at the halfway point of the penultimate month of 2026.
 This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.
 Weren't we just celebrating the return of spring? The start of summer? The first Saturday of football season? And now, we're 10 days away from Thanksgiving.
 For those with turkeys in the freezer, that means those birds need to move to the fridge around Friday. Don't make a rookie mistake and wait till next week. You're too late if you do that. A good rule of thumb: Allow 24 hours for 4-5 pounds of turkey.
 10 KITCHEN ESSENTIALS FOR A STRESS-FREE THANKSGIVING 
 I'm frying a 14-pounder next Thursday, which means it needs to be pretty much thawed by Wednesday so I can get her ready for the big day. That means I need to have it in the fridge no later than Saturday. I'll probably move her over on Friday just to be safe.
 Prepare now so you don't look like an IDIOT next week. Trust me, I've been there.
 On that note, let's roll.
 UCF Knights cheer team performs during the second half against the Arizona State Sun Devils at Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando, Fla., on Nov. 14, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 
 Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where another big weekend of college football left two fanbases asking some pretty fair questions about the state of the sport.
 YES, ALABAMA'S COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RANKING IS ABSURD, BUT ONE TEAM GOT ROYALLY SCREWED BY THE COMMITTEE 
 You'll see.
 What else? I've got my Wake Forest Demon Deacons making me look like a genius once again this past Saturday, a couple MASSIVE hits in the NFL yesterday, and AT&T Lily is BACK after a long hiatus.
 Been a while, Lil. Good to have you firing on all cylinders for the holiday season.
 OK, grab you some fast food for National Fast Food Day, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap!
 College football players have no connection to the school anymore
 I haven't had fast food in years. Years. I drive through the McDonalds or Wendy's once in a while to get a diet coke because I think fast food diet cokes are ELITE, but other than that, it's been a while since I've actually ordered any food.
 From what I can remember, the Mount Rushmore is still pretty simple:
 Taco Bell (Nothing beats a Chalupa)
 Burger King (I like going against the grain)
 Wendy's (They recently brought back the yellow cups, which earned my respect)
 McDonald's (Easily the best breakfast, but inferior everywhere else)
 I feel pretty good about this list. Again, I haven't eaten a thing from any of those places in years, but as a former fat kid, I certainly have the experience.
 OK, let's get this class started with a big weekend of college football ...
 And a troubling one:
 Ole Miss had a rough Sunday
 So, both those clips went viral over the weekend, but I'm not shocked by any of it. For years, folks have been warning us that "this is where college football is headed."
 We're not headed there any more, boys and girls. We're there. It's here.
 The NIL and transfer portal era of college football has killed these traditions. They'e done. Singing the fight song after a game is over, respecting the alma mater, it's all done.
 It's mainly because these players have absolutely NO connection to these programs anymore. None. Zero. Zilch.
 Do you know how many new players UCF has on its roster this season? Thirty-two. The year before? Forty-one. These rosters are turned over every single year. Out with the old, in with the new. It's free agency.
 LSU Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt takes the field as the Tigers face Alabama at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., on Nov. 7, 2026. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) 
 What loyalty does Sam Leavitt have to LSU? This is his THIRD team in three years (Arizona State, Michigan State). This is the price you pay for ... paying a price. The second NIL and the transfer portal were introduced, it was game over for the old college football.
 "I thought we could have a hell of a team next year, and then maybe 70 or 80 percent of the players you talk to, all they want to know is two things: What assurances do I have that I'm going to play because they're thinking about transferring, and how much are you going to pay me?"
 That's a quote from Nick Saban about his ALABAMA team the day after the Rose Bowl loss a few years ago. He warned us, and now it's here. I'm still convinced it's why he left.
 Sad.
 OK, let's stay on the college football train and head down to Norman, where Oklahoma put the final nail in Ole Miss's coffin yesterday, and the cheerleaders somehow caught a stray on the way out of town:
 Wake, Tennessee & AT&T Lily!
 "I’m here in Norman and I have to say, the fan base is insane. Grown men and women taunting the cheerleaders is embarrassing. I’m just trying to shake my pom-poms and do my job. Grown men should not be yelling at me," cheerleader Mary Ella Chicorelli said.
 "I know our student section is kind of a lot and those are college kids. But, this was grown men and women in the stands. And walking around, the pictures they were taking … it was bad. I’m glad you got a good win and could rush the field, congratulations." 
 It just means more in the SEC, I reckon. No idea what was said because Mary Ella didn't really expand upon anything, so I can't pass too much judgement here. Frankly, the Rebels have much bigger problems on their hands after yesterday's dud.
 You know who DOESN'T have any problems right now? The Wake Forest Demon Deacons! Let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big night of (crappy) FOOTBALL, and start with Wake:
 Two weeks ago, I BEGGED everyone to jump on the Wake Forest bandwagon. I vouched for the Demon Deacons after the CFP committee shafted them in the first batch of rankings, and I took some blowback.
 From Luke P. — a longtime Nightcaps reader who is a great friend of the program:
 Wake Forrest got hosed? Cmon bud GTFOH. Last 3 games vs a now 5 loss VA team, a now 6 loss Cal team, and now 4 loss NC St team that's interviewing cringy past subway ambassador for HC. Oh before that they put up big on a now 5 loss Stanford squad. I guess we'll find out if wake is real this weekend against Merrimack, who has lost to Rhode Island, Delaware, Tarleton St, Yale and Dartmouth but recently fought hard for a W over ...Wagner. ?!? 
 I'm Gobsmacked by this simple take but listen it's probably just the weather and whatever. There's not a quality win on their record. And stop with Purdue, who yup you guessed it has 5 losses sooner than later to be 7 or 8. Vegas hasn't caught up is hilarious! 
 Wake Forest Demon Deacons wide receiver Jack Foley stiff-arms Stanford Cardinal cornerback Leroy Bryant during the first half at Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium in Winston-Salem, N.C., on Oct. 3, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 
 I absolutely HAMMERED the Wake moneyline Saturday against SMU. The Demon Deacons were, somehow, an underdog! I got them at +110! I also hammered the team total, which was at 31.5. It hit in the second quarter.
 Once again, Vegas hadn't caught up. And, for the billionth time this season, I made a killing because of it.
 Wake Forest is good, folks. I'll continue to die on this hill.
 Next? You know who is NOT good? The Tennessee Titans. That being said, we can't have a Monday class without showing proper respect to Titans kicker Joey Slye .
 What a HIT:
 BOOOOOOOOOOOM! That's the football I grew up and fell in love with. We saw a couple big-time hits yesterday, and — surprisingly — none of them came with the obligatory laundry.
 THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! 
 Poor Fernando Mendoza was at the receiving end of two of them:
 Lordy. Textbook tackles. By the way, I thought Mendoza looked excellent yesterday. Feel like we all forgot just how elite he was last year given it's been nearly 11 months since we saw him play in an actual game.
 Spoiler alert: He's still good at football.
 OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week, everyone.
